subject: doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/trace-forensics.md
why: New playbook, map 2.3. Steps: (1) identify the format and load it, through delegation when parsing would flood the context; (2) dump to a queryable form before reading; (3) narrow by the artifact's shape; (4) attribute to source or state the symbols are missing; (5) confirm with a paired capture or label the strongest hypothesis; (6) closeout on every exit. Reply: a cited diagnosis handed back, no fix.

subject: doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/worktree-cleanup.md
why: New playbook, map 2.23, Git half. Steps: (1) df snapshot and audit.py, read-only, paths from Git; (2) cross-check the owner's pinned set; (3) pause on uncommitted work and show its diff; (4) propose, naming ignored files removal would delete; (5) remove what the owner approved by name, each by its exact path and never by a global prune; (6) closeout on every exit: rerun the audit and df. Reply: pruned, proposed awaiting approval, or nothing to prune.

subject: cursor_plugins:playbook:pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/worktree-cleanup
why: Map 2.23 and owner ruling 2026-11-01: the Git half, with clean and merged becoming propose, then prune on approval (AGENTS.md Authority and Safety).

modifications: Clean and merged is proposed and pruned only on approval of that worktree, never automatically.

Our own read-only audit.py, without size, PR state or chat scanning; it adds ignored-file, on-a-ref, locked and current-worktree facts, judges every worktree against one base commit resolved once in the selected repo, and holds any worktree with no base to judge by.

git worktree remove <path> for an approved worktree or prunable record, so a named approval removes only that one, never git worktree prune; without --force, so Git's own refusal stays a gate; forcing needs approval after the refusal.
Untracked files pause like tracked edits and are named, rather than being dropped as safe.
deliberately_dropped: Simulators, editor state and package caches; revisit_when: that tooling enters our toolchain.
Fanning subagents out over chat transcripts and the pinned-chat sidebar: Cursor-only, so the owner's list replaces them.

subject: doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/eval.md
why: New playbook, map 2.12, Claude Code candidates only (ruling 10). Steps: (1) frame, a judge-only rubric, and the go-ahead for the spend; (2) a sandbox template per variant; (3) one organic prompt; (4) candidates through eval/run.sh as fresh top-level sessions inside a bwrap boundary; (5) one blinded judge through delegation, from a different family by the roster; (6) the chain check through eval/classify.py, reading unproven entries by hand; (7) read every output and compare with the judge; (8) closeout on every exit. Reply: finished, stopped before any run, or stopped during the runs.

subject: cursor_plugins:playbook:pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/eval
why: Map 2.12, rows 16 and 24, and ruling 10: live for Claude Code candidates only, promoting the S8 runner and a classifier that matches each tool call to its result.

merged_from: scratchpad S8 runner and classifier (gitignored; promoted into eval/)
modifications: Candidates are fresh top-level headless sessions in a copy of a template, not subagents (R8), so one model at a time rather than parallel models.

Each candidate runs inside a required bwrap boundary, an enforced mechanism of our own: only its copy is writable at a fixed path under an empty home, the environment is an allow-list with authentication inherited, the host, other runs and the logs are out of reach, and the only network is a host-side proxy that allows the Anthropic API and logs each decision. Linux only until a candidate runs on another OS.
The judge is one critic through delegation, from a different family by the roster.

The chain check scores the candidate's own tool calls matched to their results from stream-JSON logs, with per-variant validated patterns, in place of workspace transcripts: a read must resolve to the exact file in the run's workspace, ambiguous shell evidence is unproven for a person to read, and delegates' reads are reported apart.
A go-ahead for the spend, naming the permission mode, comes before any run; bypassPermissions needs its own explicit approval (AGENTS.md, Safety).
The runner refuses a --path-prepend holding a revealing word; a prompt may name a test when the task is really about one.
deliberately_dropped: Cross-family candidates and the arena skill's phases: they wait for a second vendor's runner and event stream (ruling 10).
Cursor agent-transcripts and per-family model lines.
